items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: we worked on a couple of projects. It’s like he would call up, “Hey Frank I’m putting together a book can I get” — because we owned the rights to those articles.

ctx.x: Yeah, no. We got to know him a little bit. I did an interview with him and it was a challenge. Not ‘cause he was — he was very nice. But he was Nat Hentoff. And I felt like everything I’m asking him I hope is not like silly.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. He was a good guy. But I think he was kind of like, you know, but we worked on a couple of projects. It’s like he would call up, “Hey Frank I’m putting together a book can I get” — because we owned the rights to those articles. I said of course. And for those people we would just say yeah, those are your articles, you have the right to do that. There’s no charge for that. So we would work together on things like that. And when there was an anniversary issue we had us write some pieces for us.…
I don’t know if you’d share this with me but what’s the biggest, most significant disaster you’ve had in your tenure at DownBeat, with some kind of article or a mistake.
